For every finite Artinian lift, the O-algebra generated by all representation entries is finite local with residue k. Failure of the selected entries to span its relative cotangent gives two actual dual-number lifts contradicting the finite separation set.

Each selected-entry map is surjective by FP1. Finite-level kernels contain m_P^n and are finite in number; product images over the common residue field prove closure under intersection and uniqueness even for different representations with the same kernel.

The finite-level universal objects have compatible truncations. Compactness proves J_n=J+m_P^n, so P/J is the actual Noetherian universal ring, with continuous limit representation and unique maps to every complete target.

The near-identity characters are linearly independent over any coefficient ring: a finite Laurent relation becomes an ordinary polynomial after multiplication by a character, and the substitution T=1+u is invertible.

Finite Artinian truncation makes all relevant weight decompositions finite before passing to separated limits. It therefore proves homogeneity of the actual kernel and the intrinsic character description of weight parts, including characteristic ell weights differing by multiples of ell.
Closed weight parts, homogeneous maximal-ideal products, finite residue quotients and Nakayama give finite homogeneous ideal generators without assuming an algebraic torus representation theorem.

The small kernel is finite and discrete, so weight-part surjections have continuous sections by compactness and finite coset representatives. This proves the asserted continuity for arbitrary topologies on the local groups.

The interpolation ring A-dagger is a finite square-zero extension in the same coefficient category. Its map to A[[u]] is injective by character independence and multiplicative because I^2=0. Closedness and near-identity torus stability of the exact local condition force it to survive projection, giving a genuinely graded local representation satisfying L.

Completed coproduct, frame variables and explicit closed ideals construct the actual universal tuple. The residual tuple proves that the defining ideal is proper; no representability theorem is assumed.
